reason: The cited evidence (E1) demonstrates that N-doping a PtCoFeNiCu HEA electrocatalyst creates a Pt-rich shell, forms metal–nitrogen bonds, optimizes adsorption energies, and improves corrosion resistance. However, the hypothesis extrapolates these findings from an electrocatalytic oxygen reduction reaction environment to a fundamentally different automotive exhaust catalysis context (gas-phase, transient, low-temperature, H2O/NO exposure, thermal aging) without any cited evidence for this translation, leaving the final premise unsupported.
premises: Nitrogen doping of a multi-element alloy creates a Pt-rich surface layer
Nitrogen doping forms robust metal–nitrogen bonds within the alloy
Metal–nitrogen bonds suppress metal leaching and enhance corrosion resistance
Nitrogen doping optimizes adsorption energies for reactants/intermediates
These effects translate from electrocatalysis to automotive exhaust catalysis
